test_plan.scope: Validate FR-048..FR-056 (GET /help route, glossary entry schema, two-voice rendering, anchor deep-linking, links validator, verdict-card Learn-more link, typed filter, bootstrap content, sidebar nav) plus NFR-022..NFR-026 (performance, embed-only packaging, accessibility, SEO/discoverability, architectural boundary).
test_plan.approach: Three-layer pyramid. Unit tests pin the loader (schema validation, duplicate handling, slug regex) and pure helpers (AnchorResolver.FirstValidAnchor). Integration tests exercise help.Service end-to-end with synthetic glossary fixtures and a mocked LogFunc, verifying loader behaviour, validator output, and Renderer HTML structure via goquery. e2e tests run the real HTTP handler behind a test session against an in-process server with the production glossary embedded, plus a Playwright spec that drives the typed filter and Learn-more anchor flow against the actual rendered page. CI lint pipeline gates the architectural boundary (NFR-026) and bootstrap-content invariants (FR-055).
fixtures: fakeLogger — captures structured log lines as []LogLine{Format,Args} for assertion. Methods: Lines(), Count(substr), Last()

fixtureGlossary — testdata/glossary-*.json bundle with named subsets: minimal (1 entry per category, 5 total), full (≥30 entries matching production), missing-field-plain, invalid-category, duplicate-id, unknown-field, no-thresholds, no-source-path, slug-too-long, slug-bad-chars
fakeRuleLinks — []contract.RuleLink builder with knobs for ruleID and links slice; supports per-test variants (all-valid, one-missing, external-https, empty-links, mixed-fragments)

testServer — httptest.Server wrapping internal/server.New with the help.Service wired and a stub insights.Service.RuleLinks() returning fixture data; cookie helper newTestSession(t) returns a valid auth cookie via parent authMiddleware
tmpEmbedDir — t.TempDir() workspace used by NFR-023 integration test — invokes the built binary with no on-disk glossary file present
playwrightContext — chromium 1280x800 viewport context against testServer URL with auth cookie pre-set; supports viewport.setSize(375,667) for mobile tests
exclusions: No live Raspberry Pi tests for NFR-022 p99 budgets — p99 is verified on CI Linux runner using b.N≥1000 iterations with t.Logf-reported quantiles; the explicit Pi-class hardware run is a manual deployment-time check (DEPLOYMENT.md), not a CI gate.

No accessibility tests against headless screen readers — axe-core via Playwright covers contrast and label violations declared in NFR-024 AC-1; deeper semantic-flow review is deferred to manual review.
No cross-browser tests (Firefox, Safari) — Playwright runs Chromium only in CI. CSS :target and :has fallbacks are verified by feature-detection assertions, not by parallel browser runs.
No load test (1000+ rps) — the route is auth-gated, internal, single-Pi-operator scale; NFR-022 p99 budget is the only performance target and is met by ETag short-circuit + ~50 ms cold render.

No tests for items in no_go_zone: no admin UI, no Markdown editor, no /help/<id> deep routes, no SQLite glossary persistence, no localization, no SSE on /help, no internal/insights internal-API consumption from the help-page package.

test_cases.then: Sidebar contains exactly one <a href="/help"> with class containing 'nav-item' and visible text 'Help'; this anchor's DOM-source position is AFTER all other existing nav-item anchors (Dashboard, Docker, Services, Alerts, Network, History, Logs, Settings)
steps: Find anchor with href='/help'; assert exactly one such anchor exists
Assert that anchor's index in the anchors list is the last (== anchors.length-1)
test_cases.expected_result: Exactly 1 <a.nav-item href="/help"> with text 'Help'; its index in the nav-item ordered list is the last position

test_cases.title: On /help, the Help nav item carries active-state styling matching other active nav items
test_cases.given: Authenticated GET /help
test_cases.then: The sidebar's <a href="/help"> has the same active-state CSS class set as the dashboard's nav-item carries when on /. Active-state class detection: the rendered class string for the /help anchor includes 'nav-item-active' (or whatever active marker the existing sidebar uses; assert exact equality with the marker observed on the dashboard's active item)
steps: GET / authenticated; parse; find the active nav-item; record its full class attribute → activeClassDashboard
GET /help authenticated; parse; find <a href="/help">; record its class attribute → classHelp
Compute activeMarker = the class token (regex /nav-item-(active|current|on)/) present in activeClassDashboard
test_cases.expected_result: The class string of <a href="/help"> on /help contains the same active-marker token (e.g. 'nav-item-active') as the dashboard's active anchor on /

test_cases.title: Clicking the Help nav item navigates to /help in the same tab
test_cases.given: page on /
test_cases.then: page.url() ends with '/help'; the page is in the same browser tab (page.context().pages().length unchanged); the anchor had no target='_blank'
test_cases.expected_result: page.url() ends with /help; pages-count unchanged before vs after click; clicked anchor's target attribute is null or empty string

test_cases.title: Adding the Help nav item does NOT move, rename, or restyle any existing sidebar item
preconditions: Snapshot baselineSidebarHTML captured from a build BEFORE FR-056 (file: testdata/sidebar-baseline.html) — list of (href, label, classAttr) for each pre-existing nav-item: Dashboard '/', Docker '/docker', Services '/services', Alerts '/alerts', Network '/network', History '/history', Logs '/logs', Settings '/settings'
test_cases.given: Authenticated GET / rendered with FR-056 applied
test_cases.when: Parse the rendered sidebar; collect all nav-item anchors except href='/help'; compare to baselineSidebarHTML triples
test_cases.then: For every pre-existing href in {'/', '/docker', '/services', '/alerts', '/network', '/history', '/logs', '/settings'}: the rendered anchor's text label and class attribute are byte-equal to the baseline triple; the count of nav-item anchors with href != '/help' equals the baseline count exactly
steps: renderedItems := all <a.nav-item> with href != '/help' as map[href] = {label, classAttr}
For each href in baselineItems: assert renderedItems[href].label == baselineItems[href].label
For each href in baselineItems: assert renderedItems[href].classAttr == baselineItems[href].classAttr
test_cases.expected_result: Every existing nav-item href has byte-equal label and class attribute to its pre-FR-056 baseline; the non-help nav-item count equals the baseline count exactly — zero existing items moved, renamed, or restyled

test_cases.title: Server-side render p99 of GET /help is <500 ms over 100 sequential requests
preconditions: testServer running with production fixtureGlossary 'full' (≥30 entries)
test_cases.given: Server warmed (one initial GET /help completed); ETag cache populated
test_cases.when: 100 sequential authenticated GET /help requests are issued, each with no If-None-Match header (forces full render)
test_cases.then: The p99 of measured wall-clock durations is <500 ms; p50 is <100 ms
steps: For i in 1..100: t0=time.Now(); GET /help; durations[i] = time.Since(t0)
Sort durations; compute p50 = durations[49], p99 = durations[98]
test_cases.expected_result: p99 < 500 ms, p50 < 100 ms over 100 sequential GET /help requests

test_cases.title: Filter keystroke→visual update p99 <100 ms over 50 sequential keystrokes
preconditions: Performance.now() probe injected as in TC-HP-054h
test_cases.given: Page /help loaded; #help-filter focused
test_cases.when: Inject 50 distinct single-character keystrokes (e.g. typing 'cpufreq…' character-by-character then backspacing then typing other terms) and capture filter-delta for each
test_cases.then: p99 of filter-deltas < 100 ms; p50 < 30 ms
steps: page.evaluate to install a performance probe that records timestamps for each input event and the next style-update batch (via requestAnimationFrame chain ending after class-toggle completes)
For each of 50 keystrokes: page.keyboard.press(key); wait 100 ms; pull recorded delta
test_cases.expected_result: p99 of filter-update delta < 100 ms; p50 < 30 ms over 50 keystrokes

test_cases.title: Filter operates with ZERO additional XHR/fetch calls after initial GET /help
test_cases.given: Page /help loaded; network capture started; before any filter input
test_cases.when: Type 'cpu' character-by-character into #help-filter; clear it; type 'ram'; clear it
test_cases.then: Across all keystrokes after the initial page load completed, page.context() recorded zero requests (XHR or fetch) to any URL — the filter is fully client-side
steps: Set up requestCount=0 listener: page.on('request', () => requestCount++)
test_cases.expected_result: Zero new requests on the network panel between filter-typing start and filter-clearing end (post-initial-load)

test_cases.title: Removing on-disk glossary file after build does not change runtime behaviour — go:embed works
preconditions: tmpEmbedDir is an empty t.TempDir() with no internal/help/glossary/glossary.json
test_cases.given: Built binary copied into tmpEmbedDir; no glossary.json on disk anywhere in tmpEmbedDir
test_cases.when: The binary is started in tmpEmbedDir as its working directory; an authenticated GET /help is issued
test_cases.then: GET /help returns 200 with the same number of glossary entries as a build-tree run; the response body length matches within 1% of a control build-tree run
steps: controlBody = curl /help (in build tree, with on-disk file present)
controlEntries = count of '<article class="help-entry"' substrings in controlBody
Copy bin/ultron-ap into tmpEmbedDir; cd tmpEmbedDir
Start binary; capture testBody from authenticated GET /help
testEntries = count of article markers in testBody
test_cases.expected_result: testEntries == controlEntries; body length difference <1% — runtime behaviour unchanged when on-disk glossary is absent

test_cases.title: POST to any /help-related endpoint returns 404 — no glossary-write API exists
test_cases.given: Authenticated client
test_cases.when: POST /help with body {} AND POST /api/help/glossary with body {} AND POST /api/help/entry with body {}
test_cases.then: All three responses have status code 404 (route not registered)
steps: POST /help — assert resp.StatusCode == 404 (or 405, but Go ServeMux GET-only mux returns 405 → accept either 404 or 405)
test_cases.expected_result: POST /help → 404 or 405; POST /api/help/glossary → 404; POST /api/help/entry → 404

test_cases.title: Help-page package contains zero os.Open / os.ReadFile calls referencing glossary paths
test_cases.given: Source files under internal/help/
test_cases.when: Static analysis (go/ast or grep) scans for os.Open|os.ReadFile|os.OpenFile|ioutil.ReadFile calls in non-test files of internal/help
test_cases.then: Zero matches in production .go files (test files excluded); the only source of glossary content is the //go:embed directive on the package-level var glossaryJSON
steps: Use go/ast.ParseFile + ast.Walk to find SelectorExpr with X.Name in {os, ioutil} and Sel.Name in {Open, ReadFile, OpenFile}
Filter out comments and string literals (only function calls)
Additionally grep for '//go:embed' in non-test files; assert exactly one occurrence in the file containing var glossaryJSON []byte
test_cases.expected_result: Zero os.Open/os.ReadFile/os.OpenFile/ioutil.ReadFile calls in production code; exactly one //go:embed directive on var glossaryJSON []byte

test_cases.expected_result: Exactly 1 h1; 5 section[data-category] each with 1 header>h2; article count == svc.EntryCount(); each article has exactly 1 h3

Assert body contains 'too hot' or another snippet from the plain body of that entry

test_cases.title: Adding a new entry to glossary does not change any existing entry's URL fragment — slugs are stable
preconditions: fixtureGlossary 'baseline-3' contains exactly 3 entries with ids ['entry-cpu-percent','entry-ram-percent','verdict-thermal-throttling']
fixtureGlossary 'baseline-3-plus-1' contains the same 3 entries plus a new entry id='entry-disk-percent'
test_cases.given: Two glossary fixtures: baseline (3 entries) and extended (same 3 + 1 new)
test_cases.when: Load each fixture into help.New(fakeLogger) and collect the entry id sets
test_cases.then: The set of entry ids from baseline is a strict subset of the extended set; the difference set has exactly 1 element ('entry-disk-percent'); for each id in baseline, the entry's id field is byte-equal between the two loads
steps: Assert idsA is subset of idsB
For each id in idsA: assert svcA.EntryByID(id).ID == svcB.EntryByID(id).ID (byte-equal)
test_cases.expected_result: idsA is subset of idsB; the single new id is 'entry-disk-percent'; every baseline entry id appears byte-equal in the extended load

test_cases.given: The project's internal/help package tree
test_cases.when: Shell out: go list -deps ./internal/help/... and filter the import paths
test_cases.then: Zero lines match the regex 'github.com/cesareyeserrano/ultron-ap/internal/(insights|alerts|notify)(/|$)'
steps: If non-zero, t.Fatalf with the list of offending packages
test_cases.expected_result: go list -deps ./internal/help/... produces zero lines matching internal/(insights|alerts|notify)

test_cases.title: ValidateLinks signature accepts only []contract.RuleLink — no insights.Rule or insights.Verdict types cross the boundary
test_cases.given: Public API surface of internal/help
test_cases.when: Reflect on every exported method of help.Service
test_cases.then: For every exported method, every parameter and return type's PkgPath is either empty (builtin) OR starts with 'github.com/cesareyeserrano/ultron-ap/internal/help' OR is from the standard library; no parameter or return type's PkgPath contains '/internal/insights' or '/internal/alerts' or '/internal/notify'
steps: For each param j in 0..m.Type.NumIn()-1 and return k in 0..m.Type.NumOut()-1: t := the parameter or return type, walking through pointer/slice/map element types
For every collected type t: pkg := t.PkgPath(); assert !contains(pkg, '/internal/insights') && !contains(pkg, '/internal/alerts') && !contains(pkg, '/internal/notify')
test_cases.expected_result: No exported help.Service method exposes a parameter or return type whose package path contains internal/insights, internal/alerts, or internal/notify

test_cases.title: Help-page package contains zero call sites to alerts.*, notify.*, or telegram/email send functions
test_cases.given: Production .go files under internal/help/
test_cases.when: Static AST scan for SelectorExpr where X.Name in {alerts, notify, telegram, email, smtp} (any imported alias) — but since the boundary check already prohibits these imports, the assertion is: the imports list of every internal/help/*.go (non-test) does NOT include any of those packages
test_cases.then: For every production .go file in internal/help/: imports list is disjoint from {.../internal/alerts, .../internal/notify, anything containing 'telegram', anything containing 'smtp'}
steps: For each file: ast.ParseFile; collect Imports
test_cases.expected_result: No production .go file in internal/help/ imports a package whose path contains '/internal/alerts', '/internal/notify', 'telegram', or 'smtp'
